contract.defaults: weight defaults to 0; weights are rescaled to 1.0 when the total is more than 0.01 from 1.0
rules: portfolio must have a holdings array (the node's message: Portfolio must have holdings array)
every holding must have a ticker (the node's message: Each holding must have a ticker)
weights default to 0 and are rescaled to 1.0 when the total is more than 0.01 from 1.0
addition: holdings must be a non-empty array of objects
every weight must be present, a finite number, and not negative; the total must be positive
scenario_type, if present, must be one of the five templates; with no custom_scenario and no scenario_type the workflow's default (tech_crash) applies
custom_scenario, if present, must be a string; horizon_days, if present, must be a finite number

reasons: Portfolio must have holdings array (the node's own rule)
Portfolio must have holdings array (the node's own rule)
Each holding must have a ticker (the node's own rule)
portfolio.holdings is not iterable (the node's own rule)
holdings is a dict, not an array (gate addition)
holding 0 (NVDA) has a weight that is not a number ('0.5'): JavaScript would join it as text (gate addition)
weights total 0.0: rescaling by a zero total gives NaN weights (gate addition)
holding 1 (AMD) has a negative weight (-0.3): the engine would treat it as a short position without saying so (gate addition)
scenario_type 'meltdown' is not one of ['ai_regulation', 'black_swan', 'chip_shortage', 'rate_hike', 'tech_crash']: the workflow would silently run tech_crash (gate addition)
holdings is empty: nothing to stress-test (gate addition)
holding 1 (AMD) has no weight: the node counts it as 0 and the engine then fails on it (gate addition)
